destinations.title: Can phenomenological coupling of PST axionic quintessence to dark matter permit larger departures from cosmological-constant behavior while satisfying the paper's background-expansion and linear-growth data?

The shared setting compares two late-time expansion histories using the same present Hubble constant H0 and matter fraction ωm. Matter consists of pressureless baryons and cold dark matter; the alternative changes the dark-energy closure.
Can a late-time cosmology governed only by H0 and present matter fraction ωm accommodate a higher local Hubble constant while producing a measurable minimum of H(z) at small positive redshift?

Can canonical quintessence, including an exponential dark-matter interaction, increase the Hubble constant inferred from low-redshift observations relative to ΛCDM? The question concerns fitted expansion histories and their statistical fit, motivated by the disagreement between local and CMB-based H0 determinations.
The running vacuum is motivated as a possible dynamical dark-energy extension of ΛCDM addressing reported Hubble-rate and structure-growth tensions.

Which necessary conditions must small late-time changes to the ΛCDM expansion history satisfy to raise H0 while lowering σ8? The principal case modifies dark-energy w(z), followed by an extension allowing a small effective-gravity deformation.

Can late-time dark energy EFTs raise cosmologically inferred H0 relative to flat ΛCDM, and which features of the evolving equation of state control that displacement? The study extends perturbative Quintessence analysis to selected Horndeski models.
Does a one-parameter interacting scalar dark sector inspired by hybrid inflation fit CMB, BAO and supernova observations better than ΛCDM, and how much can it alleviate the H0 and S8 tensions?

How do DESI DR2 BAO observations constrain constant-sign and sign-switching dark-matter–dark-energy interactions, and how do the resulting coupling, H0 and S8 constraints depend on the supernova sample and calibration?
Can an evolving dark-dimension radius correlate dark-energy evolution with changing dark-matter masses and explain the apparent phantom behavior inferred from DESI DR2, CMB and supernova data?
